header.one_liner: HAL is India's largest Defence PSU and the country's principal aerospace OEM, designing and manufacturing fixed-wing combat aircraft (Tejas, Su-30MKI licence build), trainers (HTT-40), and helicopters

at_a_glance.Founded: 22 December 1940 (as Hindustan Aircraft Company; nationalised and merged into HAL in 1964)
at_a_glance.Listed: NSE: HAL | BSE: 541154 (IPO 2018; Government of India holds 89.97%); conferred 'Maharatna' CPSE status
at_a_glance.Key India role: HAL is India's largest Defence PSU and the country's principal aerospace OEM, designing and manufacturing fixed-wing combat aircraft (Tejas, Su-30MKI licence build), trainers (HTT-40), and helicopters

what_it_is.prose: HAL is India's largest Defence PSU and the country's principal aerospace OEM, designing and manufacturing fixed-wing combat aircraft (Tejas, Su-30MKI licence build), trainers (HTT-40), and helicopters (Dhruv ALH, Rudra, Prachand LCH, Light Utility Helicopter). FY2024-25 provisional revenue reached ₹30,400 crore (~US$3.6-4.0 bn) per the 62nd Annual Report. HAL is the prime contractor for the LCA Tejas Mk1A (180 aircraft on order across two IAF contracts: 83 in Feb 2021 for ₹48,000 Cr and 97 in Sep 2025 for ~₹62,700 Cr); is restarting licensed production of 12 Su-30MKI at Nashik (~₹11,000-13,500 Cr); and is lead integrator for the indigenous 5th-generation AMCA programme (entry to service post-2035). HAL also holds an Mar 2025 ₹62,700 Cr contract for 156 Prachand LCH (66 IAF + 90 Army), a Mar 2023 ₹6,838 Cr contract for 70 HTT-40 basic trainers, and a Mar 2024 ₹8,073 Cr contract for 34 ALH Dhruv Mk-III helicopters (Army + Coast Guard). AMCA prototype manufacturing is being competitively awarded with seven private firms bidding.

rows.india_status: 180 ordered across two IAF contracts (83 + 97). First batch of 5 ready for delivery Feb 2026; IAF targeting first Mk1A squadron by March 2027. Initial deliveries delayed by GE F404 engine supply disruption; HAL ordered 113 additional engines Nov 2025

Original production run of 272 completed 2020. Restart contract for 12 new aircraft valued at ~₹11,000-13,500 Cr signed Sep 2024; production at Nashik to begin 2027-28; deliveries by 2029. HAL Koraput factory to supply 30 engines/yr. Ozar overhaul plant capacity to be raised from 12 to 25 jets/yr

73 ALH Mk-III under production for Army (41), Navy (16) and Coast Guard (16). Mar 2024 MoD contract worth ₹8,073 Cr for 34 ALH Mk-III (Army + ICG). ICG has lost 2 ALH Mk-III in fatal accidents (incl. Jan 2025 crash)

Inducted 3 Oct 2022. Mar 28 2025 MoD signed two contracts totalling ₹62,700 Cr for 156 LCH Prachand (66 to IAF + 90 to Army Aviation Corps). Earlier orders: 15 LCH (IAF + Army) initial contract. Positioning as high-altitude complement/alternative to AH-64E Apache in Himalayas
Indigenous basic trainer. Cabinet approved procurement 1 Mar 2023; ₹6,838 Cr contract signed 7 Mar 2023 for 70 aircraft for IAF (~$827M, incl. equipment and training systems)

Twin-engine 5th-gen stealth fighter under development by ADA with HAL as lead production agency; first test model unveiled June 2026; expected entry into service after 2035 with >125 jets planned. Seven private firms bidding for prototype manufacturing Oct 2025
